question.title: MediMeet: Scale the Database with Read Replicas
question.description: Replace MediMeet’s overloaded SQL database with one write leader and two read replicas while preserving the existing load-balanced API tier.
question.author: Newton School

prompt.text: MediMeet lets patients search doctors, view free slots, and book appointments. The existing load balancer and three API servers are already provided. Replace the overloaded SQL database with one SQL primary and two SQL read replicas. Route every write (booking, cancellation, payment) to the primary, distribute reads (doctor search, free slots, My appointments) across the replicas, and connect the primary to each replica to show replication. This question assesses the topology, database roles, replication membership, and read/write routing. Replica lag and primary failure are observe-and-explain concepts: describe why a booking can be missing from My appointments immediately after the write, how you would provide read-after-write consistency, and what happens if the primary crashes. You are not expected to tune exact lag, write-acknowledgement, consensus, election, or failover values, and those values are not graded.
prompt.additionalContext: Assume asynchronous primary-to-replica propagation, so a replica may be briefly stale. The primary-to-replica connections are topology evidence, and the replication member selection identifies the databases in the group. The hidden run uses the stated 1,500 RPS and 90:10 mix. Exact lag values and cluster-wide acknowledgement, consensus, election, and failover controls are question-owned context; leave their defaults unless a question explicitly makes one a learning objective.

functionalRequirements.text: Keep one load balancer and three API servers as the traffic-serving layer.
Use one SQL primary that receives all writes.
Use two SQL read replicas that serve reads.
Connect the primary to each replica to show replication.
Explain how replica lag can make an immediate My appointments read miss a new booking and how to provide read-after-write consistency.
Explain what happens to reads and writes if the primary crashes before a replica is promoted.

dryRunCase.description: A low-rate public run for checking connectivity and the 90:10 request split.

scenarios.description: Run the stated 1,500 RPS with 90% reads and 10% writes.

structuralRules.description: Keep every component connected to the MediMeet architecture.

semanticRules.description: Keep the load balancer between patient traffic and the API servers.
Configure exactly one SQL database as the write leader.
Configure two SQL databases as followers.
Connect the SQL primary to both read replicas.
Serve read traffic from both configured read replicas.
Do not send write traffic to read-only followers.

rubricChecks.description: Use the supplied traffic layer with exactly three SQL database nodes.
